points.zh:
《日本侘寂美學》：（侘：wabi，寂：sabi）
Wabi-sabi is a beautiful philosophy to embed and practice in your everyday life.  At its core, wabi-sabi reminds you that life is fragile and temporary, it is as impermanent as anything else in nature, so why not give yourself permission to be just that, yourself?  As Beth Kempton wrote in her book, 《 Wabi Sabi, a Japanese Wisdom for a Perfect Imperfect Life》:    “ Put simply, wabi sabi gives you permission to be yourself. It encourages you to do your best but not make yourself ill in pursuit of an unattainable goal of perfection. It gently motions you to relax, slow down and enjoy your life. And it shows you that beauty can be found in the most unlikely of places, making every day a doorway to delight. ”  （ from Omar Itani ）

points.zh:
走下武嶺的山路
從標高3275公尺的武嶺 (台灣高山公路最高點)，
走下合歡山莊，山路平坦曲折，空氣輕薄清涼。
左側玉山箭竹揮灑一片，鋪綴著山坡成耀眼的
橘黃地毯。疏落的台灣冷杉堅韌地聳立其上。
南湖大山和中央尖山在北方天際遙遙相望。
更遠處，想必是大甲溪和蘭陽溪千年侵奪的思源
埡口吧！右側合歡山壁，層岩疊錯，肌理似畫，
削壁積雪叢叢，滴成涓涓細流。奇萊山和能高山
綿延東南天邊，在雲霧飄渺中，成嶺成脈。
不必向我述說
阿爾卑斯山的峻嶺雪峰
黃山的烟嵐雲霧
這裡呈現著獨特的景象
令人驚嘆的秀麗山色
斑駁的水層岩為證
飄浮的白雲為憑
自深邃的海底
升向3000 公尺的高度
百萬年來
這美麗的海島
便擁有這片蔚藍的天空
獨自展示著秀麗的風景
微風拂過玉山箭竹
吶吶成曲：
“ 遐e山，遐e湖，遐e田園
是我出世e所在，祖先e開墾，
寶貴e文化，咱Tioh愛繼續
Koh Kah伊保存落去，你e歷史Kap
自然e美，咱be永遠記住心內。”
註：陳芳玉女士所作「Chih把土」合唱曲的歌詞。

zh: 布拉姆斯（Johannes Brahms 1833~1897）是浪漫主義時期德國著名的作曲家，鋼琴演奏家，被稱為“新古典主義者”。在德國音樂史上，人們把巴赫，悲多芬，布拉姆斯稱爲“3B”，代表著巴洛克，古典和浪漫三個時期的重要音樂家。布拉姆斯把民歌作爲他創作的目標之一，汲取了匈牙利民族音樂的精華，以及匈牙利民間曲調素材，創作了四手聯彈《匈牙利舞曲集》，共21首。這是布拉姆斯作品中最通俗易懂，廣為流傳的樂曲。其旋律優美，裝飾性強，節奏自由，音色紛繁，速度輕快變化，有卽興性，濃郁的匈牙利民風和吉普賽民族音樂的浪漫特色。《匈牙利舞曲第五號》是其中情緒高昂，牽動心弦，最爲人喜愛的一首。

Johannes Brahms completed his 21 Hungarian Dances by 1879, and they remain one his most popular collections of music. All the dances are based on traditional Hungarian folk tunes and range from 1 minute to 6 minutes in duration. Embodying the fast and raucous Hungarian folk music that inspired this whole set of dances, No.5 is perhaps the most famous of them all. The quick tempo and memorable melodies come together to create a truly thrilling dance. The tempo starts quick and becomes even more frenzied by the end. Led by the strings, the rich and broad melody sweeps across the orchestra. As more instruments join in the intensity grows even stronger. When the percussion join in the drama of the music becomes the central point of the music. Brahms fluctuates between these boisterous sections and small quiet sections to create that light and shade in the music. A second theme is heard in the central section, but this is soon blown out of the water by the opening theme which returns with vengeance. Now even faster and more chaotic, the fully realized theme brings this famous dance to an explosive finale.
